notes: 12 frames extracted this session at native 1920x1080 (ffmpeg -frames:v 1; -q:v 2 JPEG for the two large-text slides, PNG for the ten dense UI/code/terminal frames per brief's small-text rule). Every frame was visually verified in-session against the VTT beat it anchors. 22 candidate timestamps were extracted and reviewed; the 12 selected maximize unique lesson concepts (question → tactic → closed-loop prompt → loop closing live → stacked validation → templated plans → ADW test node → out-loop trigger/trace/payoff). Talking-head and B-roll beats are intentionally unframed with designed-diagram guidance below.

frames.label: core-validation-question
frames.vtt_anchor: 1:37–1:53 "Given a unit of valuable work that's production ready, how would you, the engineer, test and validate this work?"
frames.why_for_weak_student: The entire lesson hangs off this one question, shown as a two-line slide (green 'valuable work', yellow 'test and validate this work?'). A weak student should be able to recite it before touching any tooling.
frames.verified_visual: Black slide, two lines: 'Given a unit of valuable work that's production ready / How would you, the engineer, test and validate this work?' with color emphasis.

frames.label: tactic-always-add-feedback-loops
frames.vtt_anchor: 3:42–3:50 "The lesson five tactic is always add feedback loops."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The official Tactic #5 card (lesson-position dots with 05 highlighted) plus the Daily Actions sidebar — a complete, memorizable summary of the tactic on one screen: add validation commands to every agentic prompt; request/validate/resolve; e2e tests for self-validation; chain feedback mechanisms; compute spent on testing buys confidence.
frames.verified_visual: 'Always Add Feedback Loops' Tactic slide, TAC laptop art left, Daily Actions list right, footer 'Close The Loops: More Compute, Higher Confidence'.

frames.label: github-issue-is-the-prompt
frames.vtt_anchor: 10:55–11:30 "I'm gonna hit new issue. This is my trigger... I'm gonna type this ADW plan build test... feature... create a new button"
frames.why_for_weak_student: The out-loop trigger artifact verbatim: title 'Random Natural Language Query', body 'adw_plan_build_test' + '/feature' + a mid-level prompt (generate-random-query button, use llm_processor.py, two-sentence limit). Shows exactly how little text kicks off a full plan→build→test pipeline — the issue IS the prompt.
frames.verified_visual: GitHub disler/tac-5 New Issue form with full trigger text and Create button; workflow selector line 'adw_plan_build_test' on line 1.

frames.label: agent-machine-webhook-trigger
frames.vtt_anchor: 11:51–12:14 "Our agent has full control over this machine... we are listening to our GitHub webhooks... you're going to see this kickoff as that webhook event comes in"
frames.why_for_weak_student: PITER's T and E made physical: the dedicated 'IndyDevDanAgents's Mac mini' window running `uv run adws/adw_triggers/trigger_webhook.py` (port 8001, POST /gh-webhook, GET /health, uvicorn) while the GitHub issue is being drafted in the foreground. Kills the abstraction anxiety about what a 'dedicated agent environment' actually is.
frames.verified_visual: Screen-shared Mac mini terminal with webhook server startup log over the New Issue page.

frames.label: first-closed-loop-prompt
frames.vtt_anchor: 13:38–14:21 "Let's write our first closed loop prompt... we have our request, we have our validation and then we have our resolution"
frames.why_for_weak_student: The simplest possible closed-loop prompt, 3 lines, verbatim: 'Update @app/server/core/sql_processor.py comment out validation.' + 'Validate your work with `cd app/server && uv run ruff check .`. If there are errors at all, resolve them.' Request → Validate → Resolve in its minimum viable form — the artifact to copy before scaling anything.
frames.verified_visual: VS Code untitled markdown buffer with the 3-line prompt; sql_processor.py tab open; Tokens: 38 in status bar.

frames.label: ruff-closes-the-loop
frames.vtt_anchor: 16:21–16:31 "We can't have load env above an import. Ruff found this. So it was passed right into the standard in of our agent and our agent is going to move this."
frames.why_for_weak_student: A loop actually closing on camera: the 3-validator prompt (ruff / pytest / py_compile) at top, Ruff's E402 'Module level import not at top of file' error in the terminal, and the agent's own words 'I need to fix the ruff errors... load_dotenv() is being called before all imports... move it after all the imports.' Tool stdout became agent context became a fix — the whole tactic in one screenshot (note 'Bypassing Permissions' = YOLO mode).
frames.verified_visual: Claude Code terminal inside VS Code: Bash(ruff check) E402 output with code excerpt, agent reasoning paragraph, prompt with 3 validation bullets above.

frames.label: pytest-catches-sabotage
frames.vtt_anchor: 16:55–17:07 "It sees that the validate SQL query has been commented out... without knowing what we previously did, right, thanks to the context window clearing, it fixed this issue"
frames.why_for_weak_student: The lesson's proof moment: a FRESH agent (context cleared) running pytest discovers the sabotage planted by the previous prompt — diff shows '# validate_sql_query(sql_query)' restored to 'validate_sql_query(sql_query)' and the SQLSecurityError import re-added, then pytest re-runs. Validators encode standards that survive across agents; no memory required.
frames.verified_visual: Update(core/sql_processor.py) diff re-enabling validation + 'Now let's run pytest again' + pytest session header in Claude Code terminal.

frames.label: full-validation-prompt-e2e
frames.vtt_anchor: 19:39–21:11 "We've now turned this into a full reusable prompt... We're running the Playwright MCP server to run the simple validation workflow... confirm seven results are returned"
frames.why_for_weak_student: The scaled-up artifact in full: '# Validation' with Backend Validation (ruff, pytest, py_compile), Frontend Validation (bun tsc --noEmit, bun run build), and E2E Validation — 6 numbered Playwright steps: open localhost:5173, screenshot ./e2e_before.png, type 'select newest 7 products sort by price desc', Query, screenshot ./e2e_after.png, read both images and confirm 7 results. This is the bridge from toy prompt to reusable codebase asset.
frames.verified_visual: 30-line # Validation markdown with all three sections and the top instruction 'Run them in order top to bottom... stop and resolve them immediately then rerun every validation step.'

frames.label: bug-plan-validation-commands
frames.vtt_anchor: 28:53–29:40 "We have validation commands... templated into the plans that get generated by our agent... If you create an end to end test, include the following validation steps"
frames.why_for_weak_student: Templated engineering made visible: bug.md's Plan Format with the '## Validation Commands' block ('Execute every command to validate the bug is fixed with zero regressions'), the conditional E2E-test task placeholder, and the three default commands (uv run pytest / bun tsc --noEmit / bun run build). Every future plan inherits feedback loops by default — 'always' is enforced by the template, not by discipline.
frames.verified_visual: bug.md Plan Format section lines 70–91 with Validation Commands template and e2e conditional; commands/ tree in explorer.

frames.label: adw-test-resolution-loop
frames.vtt_anchor: 40:56–41:21 "we're going to run tests with resolution... run front end back in tests and return a standardized JSON format so that we can automate agents"
frames.why_for_weak_student: The deterministic shell around the agentic loop: adw_test.py's run_tests_with_resolution signature (max_attempts = MAX_TEST_RETRY_ATTEMPTS) and the while attempt < max_attempts loop with run_tests(adw_id, logger) circled — plus the adws/ module tree and the issue-111/issue-222 specs in the explorer. Python owns retries and counting; agents own judgment. That division is the ADW idea.
frames.verified_visual: adw_test.py lines ~411–448 in editor, green circle on run_tests call, explorer showing adw_modules/adw_tests/adw_triggers and untracked issue-111-adw-adw111 / issue-222-adw-adw222 specs.

frames.label: agent-log-trace-500
frames.vtt_anchor: 48:22–48:47 "API error 500... it was our end to end test resolver iteration one. It ran this prompt, tried to resolve cloud code failing, which it just can't."
frames.why_for_weak_student: Observability payoff: inside the agent sandbox, the agents/ce364af1/ tree (adw_build, adw_plan, adw_test, e2e_test_resolver_iter1_0, e2e_test_runner_0_0/0_1/0_2, issue_classifier, plan_finder, pr_creator, sdlc_planner, sdlc_implementor...) with the resolver's prompts/resolve_failed_e2e_test.txt open: test_complex_query, status failed, error 'Test execution error: Claude Code error'. Every agent that ran left an inspectable trail keyed by ADW ID — that's how the 500 got diagnosed in seconds.
frames.verified_visual: Mac mini VS Code, branch feature-issue-28-adw-ce364af1-..., ce364af1 agent directory tree with resolver prompt JSON payload open.

frames.label: feature-shipped-pr
frames.vtt_anchor: 49:33–49:55 "you can see we have that new feature generate random query... it generated quite a complex query there to give this result"
frames.why_for_weak_student: The out-loop payoff: PR 'feat: #28 - Random Natural Language Query #29' files view behind the agent machine's own browser at localhost:5173, where the new Generate Random Query button produced a genuinely complex WITH/CTE SQL query and a results table — all planned, built, and tested off-device. The human's job now: the test on top of the tests.
frames.verified_visual: PR #29 files page + agent-machine browser with Query Results (city/signup_month/monthly_signups rows) and circled SQL.
